title: Disneyland and California Adventure, Anaheim, California
seoTitle: Charter Bus to Disneyland, Anaheim: Group Trip Guide
excerpt: A charter bus to Disneyland and California Adventure keeps a large group together from the hotel to the gate. Drop-off, vehicle sizing and how to plan the day.

body.text: Two parks, one esplanade between them, and a group that needs to arrive together, stay together and leave together at the end of a fourteen-hour day. That is the real problem a charter bus to Disneyland and California Adventure solves. Anaheim is not hard to drive to; it is hard to park at, hard to reassemble a group in, and expensive to do either badly.
Why a coach beats a car convoy here specifically

Disneyland's parking structures charge per vehicle per day, which multiplies quickly across a group in six cars, and they deposit you a tram ride away from the gate. A chartered vehicle uses the designated bus drop-off and puts the group on the esplanade directly. On the way out, at eleven at night with tired children, the difference between one known meeting point and six cars in four levels of a parking structure is the whole evening.

The other advantage is the return. Most groups underestimate how finished everyone is after a full park day. On a coach, the drive home is quiet and nobody is doing it on four hours of sleep and a churro.

Disneyland and Disney California Adventure are separate parks with separate gates, facing each other across a shared plaza. A one-day, one-park ticket is enough for a first visit with a large group — moving thirty people between parks costs an hour that could have been spent on rides.
If you have two days, do one park each day rather than park-hopping. Groups that hop spend a surprising amount of the day walking and re-queuing at gates.
Planning a park day for a group

items: Set a hard departure time and a named meeting point before anyone walks through the gate. 'By the flagpole at nine' works; 'we'll text' does not, in a park where cell networks are saturated.
Split into small parties with a designated adult each. Thirty people will not ride anything together, and pretending otherwise wastes the morning.
Buy tickets in advance and check whether a park reservation is required for your date — the requirement has changed repeatedly, so verify it rather than assuming.
Build in a sit-down meal. It is the only reliable way to get the whole group in one place mid-day, and it is worth booking ahead.
Plan the exit. Fireworks end with tens of thousands of people leaving simultaneously; either leave fifteen minutes early or plan to wait half an hour.

body.text: Which charter bus fits a Disneyland group

items: Forty to fifty-six: a full-size [charter bus](/fleet/motor-coaches) is the standard vehicle for school, church and youth groups, with luggage bays for a multi-day trip and an on-board restroom for the drive.
Twenty to thirty-two: a [mini bus](/fleet/mini-buses) suits a family reunion or a smaller youth group and maneuvers more easily around the Anaheim hotel district.
Ten to fourteen: a [sprinter van](/fleet/sprinter-vans) works for an extended family or a corporate incentive group.
Under ten: an [SUV](/fleet/suvs) covers airport transfers for a small party without committing to a larger vehicle.

body.text: School and youth groups are the majority of what we run into Anaheim, and our [school trip transportation](/services/school-trips) quotes come with the insurance certificates and driver documentation districts require.

John Wayne Airport is about fifteen minutes away and Los Angeles International around forty-five without traffic, which is a meaningful qualifier on a weekday afternoon. Our [airport transfer service](/services/airport-transfers) tracks flight numbers rather than scheduled times, which matters when a group is arriving on three different flights.

Most Anaheim hotels near the resort are within walking distance or a short hop, and many have coach loading areas. Groups searching for charter bus rental near me for a Disneyland trip should ask whether the vehicle stays on site for the day or returns later — a coach waiting locally can collect a tired half of the group at four while the rest stay for fireworks, which is frequently the difference between a good trip and a long one. We run pickups from [Anaheim](/locations/california/anaheim), [Los Angeles](/locations/california/los-angeles) and across Southern California.

Mid-January to mid-March and mid-September to mid-November are the quietest windows, with the shortest queues and the lowest prices. Summer, spring break and the stretch from Thanksgiving to New Year are the busiest and the most expensive. For a large group the crowd calendar matters more than the weather does — the parks are pleasant year-round, but a queue that is twenty minutes in February is ninety in July.

One last piece of advice from groups who do this every year: agree the rules about splitting up before the trip, not in the parking lot. Who can go where unaccompanied, what the check-in times are, and what happens if someone misses one. Ten minutes of that conversation on the bus, while everyone is still in one place and listening, prevents almost every problem a large group has inside a theme park.

Send your dates, headcount, hotel and the time you want to be at the gate, plus your intended departure time. [Request an all-in quote](/quote) and you will usually have an itemized price back the same day, driver, fuel, tolls and taxes included.
